body: How did you try to save your data?

Instead of

```
DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE 
```

I would recommend using the built in "modified" behavior of the model using a datetime field "modified" and `DEFAULT NULL`.
It will automatically update itself with each save.

http://book.cakephp.org/2.0/en/models/saving-your-data.html#using-created-and-modified
I understand a reason, but this is a bug.
It's more a limitation of 2.x's ORM. I doubt it's going to be changed.
We could set the schema default to '' when the column type is timestamp and the default value is CURRENT_TIMESTAMP when reflecting schema. That would fix this issue, but possibly cause others.

issue.title: Datetime current_timestamp issue

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
Cakephp 2.x

``` sql
CREATE TABLE `test` (
  `id` int(11) unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `created` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
 ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8;
```

Related to issue 4184
https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/4184
and pull 4386
https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/pull/4386/files

Since The `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` support for a `DATETIME` datatype was added in MySQL 5.6 and cakephp only checks `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` for a `TIMESTAMP datatype like this:

``` php
if ($fields[$column->Field]['type'] === 'timestamp' && strtoupper($column->Default) === 'CURRENT_TIMESTAMP') {
    $fields[$column->Field]['default'] = '';
}
```

So it will not work with a DATETIME datatype.

I know there is a lot of word around and cakephp will do everything if I remove CURRENT_TIMESTAMP but may be it will be better work with  a DATETIME datatype.

issue.title: Fixing 'default current_timestamp' in Sqlite

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
Some of my Sqlite tables have `datetime` or `timestamp` columns with `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` set - if there values are omitted, the current timestamp is filled in by the database. 
But due to a bug in Sqlite, `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` is detected as default value, and interpreted as a string. When creating a new record, CakePHP writes this string to the database, and not the current time. 

This problem has also been present in Mysql, and has been fixed there in #4184. I ported the fix (and the corresponding testcase) from 7936b5e7642935983833e3ea28ddafe4f3d84e08 to Sqlite.
